facts.label: Achar produtos
facts.sub: Pergunte Where can I find + produto? e responda com It’s in aisle + número ou It’s on the top shelf. Para ler placas, use What does that sign say?

facts.label: Corredor
facts.sub: Nos supermercados dos EUA, cada corredor tem número e placa com os produtos. Frases como “Aisle six” e “Check aisle two” são muito ouvidas.

facts.label: Placas
facts.sub: As placas amarelas ou azuis ficam acima dos corredores e mostram as categorias de produtos, como dairy, canned goods, snacks e bakery. Ler a placa é o jeito mais rápido de achar o que você procura.

compare.us: In the USA, aisle numbers and signs are very clear. Workers say “Aisle six” and point.

pages.title: Looking for rice · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday morning at a big supermarket in Orlando. Darius pushes a cart and looks at a long shopping list. He stops next to an employee. “**Excuse me, where can I find rice?**” he asks.
“**Check aisle number six,**” says the employee. “How do I know which aisle it is?” asks Darius. “**Look at the signs above,**” she says. There are big yellow signs over every aisle.

pages.title: Looking for rice · 2/3
paragraphs: “**What does that sign say?**” Darius asks. “Canned goods and pasta,” she reads. “And the next one?” “Dairy and eggs.” “**Where is the bread?**” he asks. “It is in aisle two, next to the bakery.”

Darius walks to aisle six and finds the rice. There are white rice, brown rice and black beans. “**Do you also sell brown rice?**” he asks. “Yes. **The brown rice is on the top shelf,**” she says. Darius is short, so he asks her to help.

paragraphs: She takes a bag and puts it in his cart. “Thank you! Aisle numbers are very helpful,” says Darius. “You’re welcome. Have a nice day!” He checks his list again: rice, bread, eggs and milk. Ten minutes later, his cart is full and he walks to the register.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Shelf e shop começam com o som “sh”, que muitos brasileiros trocam por “ch” (“chelf”, “chop”).
pages.how: Arredonde os lábios e solte ar contínuo: “shhh”. Em shelf, siga com “elf”: “shelf”.
pages.tip: Faça “shhh” como pedindo silêncio e acrescente a vogal sem parar o ar.
